per_shot.note: The wing entrance is a near-black pillar with a tiny GALLERY placard and an unlit magenta void beyond; the showpiece does not announce itself from the hall, and a pink reflection blob on the right floor reads as a smear.

Reads as a museum: overhead spot cones, glass vitrines, readable placards, and a coloured light pool under each stone. The plinth bodies sink to black and the mirror-floor streaks dominate the lower half.

Tank light lands on the floor and ceiling in each tank's world hue and the room feels alive. The creatures are thin, pale and low-contrast against their own glow, the tanks are empty of habitat, and the glass barely reads apart from the rims.

top_issues.issue: Floor reflections are too strong and streaky
top_issues.why: Long vertical colour smears fill the bottom 40% of the frame and pull the eye away from the stones and tanks. They read as a wet mirror rather than hab floor plating, and they flatten the floor's material.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Cut the reflection strength and roughen it so each source gives a soft pool rather than a long streak. Keep the coloured pool directly under each plinth or tank, and let the plate seams and value variation of the floor show through.

top_issues.issue: Vivarium creatures are faint ghosts in empty tanks
top_issues.why: The creatures are drawn as thin, pale, near-wireframe shapes that wash out against the tank glow, so at play size the Rimewing, the serpent and the Riptide barely read as themselves. Each tank is uniform glowing fluid with no rock, ice or brine floor, so nothing ties a creature to its world.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each creature a brighter emissive core and a darker or denser body against a slightly dimmer tank fill, so the silhouette pops. Add a low faceted habitat base per tank (amber rock, ice shards, nacre growth) lit by the creature, so the creature's light lands on something inside the tank.

top_issues.issue: Gallery plinths and the lower wall vanish into black
top_issues.why: The spot cones stop at the vitrine, so the plinth bodies and the lower wall are near-black. The stones float, and the museum-plinth read is weaker than the brief's 'plinths, glass, placards' asks for.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let each spot spill down onto a lighter plinth top and front face (stone or brushed metal) with a falloff to darker at the base. Give the back wall a soft warm pool behind each case so the plinth silhouettes separate from it.

top_issues.issue: The wing threshold in the hall is a dead dark slab
top_issues.why: From the hall, the Gallery doorway is a black column with an illegible sign and an unlit magenta haze behind it. The wings are meant to be showpieces, but the hall gives no hint of what lies beyond.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Light the door frame and place a readable sign, and let some of the gallery's spot-lit colour spill through the opening onto the hall floor, so the wing pulls the player east.

top_issues.issue: Mixed coloured light muddies the shared back wall and ceiling
top_issues.why: Neighbouring glows overlap into murky purple-brown on the wall between cases. The individual pieces lose their own colour identity, and the wall has no material read.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tighten each source's falloff radius so the pools stay separate, with darker gaps between them. Keep a neutral warm base light on the wall panels so seams and ribs still read between the pools.

protect: The Gallery's spotlight cones, glass vitrines and placards: an immediately legible museum read
A coloured light pool on the floor under each stone and tank, matching its hue; the light lands
The Vivarium tanks tinting the ceiling and the ribs in their own world hues
Tank colours follow the world hue families (amber, ice-cyan, sea-green, violet)
The portholes with dusk light in the Gallery wall: they tie the wing to the hab
The suit stays the brightest, most legible thing in every frame
The side-view camera and the low-poly faceted stones and creatures
